title: How To Get Students To Focus Longer Than A TikTok Video
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Michael Linsin offers a five-step strategy for training students to concentrate for longer stretches of independent work. The steps are to teach in greater, more specific detail, model even the most basic actions, check for understanding repeatedly before releasing students to work alone, start with short work periods that guarantee success, and lengthen the work time a little every day. He compares the gradual increase to exercise, where the load rises daily. Linsin claims that applied consistently the approach will transform a class within about six weeks, and he stresses that it depends on solid classroom management, highly detailed lessons and effective modeling. The emphasis throughout is on student success and full autonomy during independent practice.
points: Teaching in greater detail draws students deeper into a subject and holds attention in a jump-cut world.
Modeling the most basic actions, such as how to hold a pencil, creates small early successes that focus the mind.
Teachers should check understanding several times so students know exactly what to do without help.
Independent work time should begin at a length students can succeed at, even five minutes.
Increasing work time slightly each day, like progressive exercise load, builds sustained focus.
quotes: Teaching in greater detail is interesting to students. It causes them to pay better attention initially, but also has a way of drawing them deeper into the subject.

Cut every hurdle to success down as low as possible by answering every question, crossing every T, and preforming multiple checks of understanding before giving students the green light to work alone.
You must prepare your students to sit silently and complete the work entirely on their own.
If they have the focus of a fruit fly, then your independent practice time should initially be short.
Like exercise, you must increase the load every day. If their work time was ten minutes the day before, make it 12 minutes.
Push a little farther each day and you won’t recognize your class in six weeks.
Yes, it takes solid classroom management. (What doesn’t?) It also takes highly detailed lessons, effective modeling, and double-checking for understanding.
